representations.name: integer slack plus one algebraic remainder cell
representations.new_information: Stores floor(S_m) unit carriers and one globally unique remainder omega=S_m-floor(S_m), with a named owner and sign.
representations.repairs_loss: Prevents irrational slack from being copied once per colour and separates integer matching capacity from real analytic debt.
representations.first_test: Odd-n threshold: attempt to pay two independent demands from the same omega; the representation must expose the reuse.
representations.public_effect: Could repair M809C-05 only if omega is eliminated by one strict integer inequality.

representations.name: fractional carrier polytope with integral-demand faces
representations.new_information: Assigns nonnegative real mass to actual carriers, keeps per-carrier capacity, per-demand incidence, and the exact total S_m.
representations.repairs_loss: Distinguishes a legitimate weighted atomization from an anonymous scalar mass.
representations.first_test: Use three demands adjacent to two unit carriers and an isolated fractional remainder; fractional feasibility must not be promoted to an integral matching.
representations.public_effect: A total-unimodularity theorem could turn weighted slack into exact payment.

representations.name: rounding-error cut ledger
representations.new_information: Records for every demand cut the integer capacity floor(S_m) and the one global discrepancy epsilon_S, rather than rounding each local inequality.
representations.repairs_loss: Makes accumulation of rounding loss across circuits auditable.
representations.first_test: Glue many disjoint circuits sharing the same global S_m; any bound charging epsilon_S per circuit is killed.
representations.public_effect: Could prove all integer Hall cuts from a real global bound with one strict margin.

representations.name: mixed-anchor C7 path complex
representations.new_information: For each mixed colour retains its low cross edge, unique high internal anchor, endpoints, and the actual length-five completion paths witnessing pairwise C7 compatibility.
representations.repairs_loss: Restores the graph geometry erased by the scalar I_mix count.
representations.first_test: On the n=14 tight graph, enumerate whether two anchors reuse an internal vertex or completion edge so that scalar compatibility fails jointly.
representations.public_effect: A large compatible subcomplex would directly meet ceil(Phi).

representations.name: low-edge/high-anchor exchange graph
representations.new_information: Connects an internal-low edge to a mixed high anchor only when one can be exchanged for the other while retaining a distinct colour and an actual C7 completion.
representations.repairs_loss: Provides a typed cross-channel operation instead of adding e(A_<q*) and I_mix.
representations.first_test: Construct alternating low/high chains with a common bottleneck anchor; reject rank addition when augmenting paths collide.
representations.public_effect: A matching of size ceil(Phi) gives the direct colour exit.

representations.name: anchor-conflict graph with degree certificates
representations.new_information: Vertices are mixed colours and edges record failure of simultaneous C7 compatibility, decorated by the exact endpoint or missing path causing conflict.
representations.repairs_loss: Turns the missing cross-channel theorem into an independence-number problem with graph-derived conflict degrees.
representations.first_test: Clique-chain and complete common-bottleneck models test whether conflict degree can be large despite low scalar residue.
representations.public_effect: An independence set of order ceil(Phi) closes directly.

representations.name: rectangle-to-new-reserve switch certificate
representations.new_information: A certificate contains one owned A diagonal, its anticomplete rectangle, one explicitly absent B pair, and a local C7 argument making that B pair a legal previously unused reserve carrier.
representations.repairs_loss: Creates the target-shore atom that conditional Hall previously assumed.
representations.first_test: Apply to the graph-realizable three-demand/two-token circuit; if every licensed B pair is already occupied, the rule is killed.
representations.public_effect: One new carrier per deficient circuit would repair the exact B deficit.

representations.name: alternating carrier-creation path
representations.new_information: Tracks a path alternating between occupied B reserve atoms, owned A diagonals, and local rectangle switches, ending at a genuinely free B/slack atom.
representations.repairs_loss: Separates rearrangement of existing carriers from creation of a new one.
representations.first_test: Closed alternating cycles and the common-two-token circuit must not be counted as augmenting paths.
representations.public_effect: A path from every Hall-deficient component increases matching rank.

representations.name: boundary missing-pair creation map
representations.new_information: Maps each mixed-anchor endpoint configuration to a concrete missing pair on the B boundary, retaining endpoint degrees, colour, and reserve membership.
representations.repairs_loss: Tests whether graph realizability forces unused carriers rather than merely compatible colours.
representations.first_test: Rectangular blow-ups with identical B boundaries test unbounded collisions of the creation map.
representations.public_effect: A bounded-fibre map with a sharp enough constant could pay the residual.

representations.name: typed circuit-overlap hypergraph
representations.new_information: Hyperedges are minimal Hall circuits; vertices separately encode A owners, occupied B carriers, created carriers, and the global rounding cell.
representations.repairs_loss: Detects reuse of one owner, carrier, or irrational remainder across several locally valid conversions.
representations.first_test: Crossing circuits sharing one A diagonal and one B token must retain deficiency after every ownership-preserving uncrossing.
representations.public_effect: An acyclic or bounded-overlap decomposition would globalize local creation.
